test_title: SSC CHSL Tier-1 2023: Official Paper (Held On: 17 Aug, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following components is NOT related to the New India Literacy Programme?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Business and Enhancing skill Development**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Business and Enhancing skill Development component **is NOT related to the** New India Literacy Programme**.
 
• The government has initiated the **"New India Literacy Programme" (NILP)**, a Centrally Sponsored Scheme, set to run over five years from FYs 2022-23 to 2026-27.
 
• With a total financial outlay of Rs. 1037.90 crore, comprising a Central share of Rs. 700.00 crore and a State share of Rs. 337.90 crore, the scheme aims to target 5.00 crore non-literates aged 15 years and above.
 
• **NILP comprises five key components: Foundational Literacy and Numeracy, Critical Life Skills, Vocational Skills Development, Basic Education, and Continuing Education.**
 
• Beneficiaries are identified through door-to-door surveys conducted via a Mobile App by designated surveyors in the States/UTs.
 
• Alternatively, non-literates can register directly from any location via the mobile app to avail scheme benefits. Notably, the scheme hinges on volunteerism for teaching and learning, with volunteers able to register through the mobile app for this purpose.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The scheme is primarily technology-driven and relies heavily on online platforms for implementation. 
 
• Teaching and learning materials and resources are accessible through the DIKSHA platform of NCERT via mobile apps. 
 
• Additionally, alternative dissemination modes such as television, radio, and Samajik Chetna Kendra are also employed to spread Foundational Literacy and Numeracy. 
 
• The scheme is inclusive, targeting all non-literates aged 15 years and above, ensuring widespread access to its benefits.
